title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 69
paragraphs: This is what the Cleisthenes of Sicyon had done; and the Athenian Cleisthenes, who was his daughter's son and named after him, I suppose despising the Ionians as his namesake had despised the Dorians, imitated him so that the Athenians might not have the same tribes as the Ionians. For at this time, when he added to his own party the whole body of the Athenian common people—whom before he had despised—he changed the names of the tribes and made them greater in number than they had been; he made in fact ten tribe-rulers instead of four, and in tens also he distributed the demes among the tribes. Having added the common people to his party, he was far superior to his opponents.
